system.biography:
Background

Embraced against his will in 1770 by Sir Edward Scott (who fed on him while fleeing pursuers and does not recall the encounter), Akawa is a Plains Indian warrior turned Anarch elder who now leads the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers}, one of Milwaukee's two dominant Anarch gangs. He has learned Scott's true identity as his sire but has said nothing — a secret he holds in reserve, believing "this will be his undoing." A calm, deliberate tactician among the more impulsive Anarchs, Akawa can shapeshift into a wolf form and prefers this guise when leading the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers}. He commands total loyalty from his gang, including his volatile childe Wrecker, and wages a running turf war against Turk's rival gang, the Union.

Roleplaying Hints

Serious and grim, speaking in old-fashioned turns of phrase ("sunrises" instead of "days," "the final sleep" instead of death). Calm, observant, and in control — his patience and plotting are worthy of an Elder twice his age.
system.notes: Sire: Sir Edward Scott (unaware of the connection). Childe: Wrecker. Haven: none fixed; moves with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers}. Disciplines as printed: Animalism 2, Celerity 4, Fortitude 3, Potence 3, Presence 2, Protean 4 (capped above to this system's 1-5 scale).

system.description: You focus your preternatural speed into the smallest of motions, allowing feats of fine manipulation beyond mortal (or even ordinary Cainite) capability, such as micro-precise crafting or delicate surgery. Spend two Blood Traits and a Willpower Trait, then spend five minutes in a trance-like state of concentration. For the next five minutes you gain two free retests on all challenges related to precision, fine manipulation, or moving something without disturbing its surroundings. Any actions that do not involve fine manipulation require you to bid an additional Trait, and you lose all ties on any challenge involving gross physical movement, including combat.

Calling upon her preternatural speed, a Kindred using this power appears to undertake several actions at once, “flickering” from one action to the next. This is particularly useful in combat, as one's foe cannot guess which of the actions he perceives is the one with which the character follows through. The character seems to be a dervish while this power is in effect, beginning countless feints, dodges and parries.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait to activate this power. For the turn in which the character calls upon this power, she may use six additional Physical Traits (Graceful x2, Nimble x2, Quick x2) for the purposes of defense. These bonus Traits do not apply to the character's attacks. She also gains a single “Stutter” retest in any challenge, applicable for defensive actions. The Stutter retest is always the last retest declared in a challenge, unless the attacker declares the use of Might.

The vampire disperses into one small creature per current Blood Trait spent (or fewer, larger creatures sharing Blood Traits evenly). Lasts until sunrise or voluntary reformation; any creatures not reabsorbed by dawn are destroyed. Difficult to represent at the table — Storytellers should plan in advance how a single player represents a swarm.

The vampire can assume the exact form of the last creature (human, Cainite or animal) whose blood she has drunk. She gains none of the target's Disciplines, knowledge or Abilities, but otherwise becomes a perfect physical imitation, letting her briefly pass as someone else or, in animal form, shed the telltale stench of undeath.

System: After drinking the target's blood, the player spends two Blood Traits to transform (taking two turns, or one turn for a third Blood Trait) and rolls Manipulation + Subterfuge. Each success sustains the disguise for roughly an hour; the player may spend an additional Blood Trait to extend the deception by another hour, blood permitting. A botch means the transformation fails and the vampire can never again imitate that particular target. The assumed form holds up against all detection, including supernatural senses that would reveal a vampire's true nature, though it will not conceal the vampire's actual emotional state from senses that read emotion. The transformation automatically ends at dawn.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book One: Animals
system.bloodCost: 2 (3 to halve transformation time), plus 1 per additional hour

system.description: In challenges of strength, you may use Potence itself as your bid Trait, which can never be lost outright, though wounds or Negative Traits can still force you to risk other Traits.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: You may use the Bomb symbol in challenges of strength, which defeats Rock and Paper, ties with other Bombs, and loses only to Scissors, requiring no expenditure.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By uttering an animal call, you summon nearby animals of a chosen type to your side, favorably disposed toward you, by spending a Social Trait per animal summoned.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines
